page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance running on KVM hypervisor architecture. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7H12 processor operating at 2.6 GHz, this instance supplies 16 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory totals 32.0 GB, yielding a ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. Supported instruction sets include AVX, AES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, whereas AVX-512 extensions are absent. The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps and includes no bundled local NVMe storage or dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate average multi-core CPU throughput alongside single-core and memory bandwidth limitations. Single-core execution in stress-ng testing ranks in the lower 10th percentile with a score of 765.19, while multi-core CPU performance reaches an average rating of 6127.45. Memory bandwidth exhibits a notable contrast: cached 16 KB read operations achieve 800.3 GB/sec, but uncached 256 MB large-block transfers drop to the bottom 25th percentile at 29.73 GB/sec for reads and 15.34 GB/sec for writes. Synthetic workloads such as Geekbench (1305.0 single-core, 7305.0 multi-core) and PassMark CPU score (18931.51) consistently align with middle 50th percentile performance across compilation, image processing, and encryption metrics.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c6a.4xlarge offers resource density tailored for scale-out compute tasks requiring dedicated core access rather than high single-threaded throughput or uncached memory capacity. Performance in application-specific benchmarks includes static web serving throughput of 6.53 GB/sec and Redis SET performance of 14.19 million operations per second. Lacking local storage and high uncached memory bandwidth, this instance is primarily suited for distributed worker nodes, software compilation, static web serving, microservices, and general batch compute jobs.
